name: Digital Lending — Approved Partner Structural Check
sourceDocument: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
supersedes: Guidelines on Digital Lending (September 2, 2022, RBI/2022-23/098 DOR.CRE.REC.66/03.10.001/2022-23)
issuer: Reserve Bank of India, Department of Regulation
clauseStatus: PRIMARY SOURCE CONFIRMED; NO BOARD-APPROVED-LSP-LIST REQUIREMENT
clauseStatusDetail: The official RBI notification confirms current RE-LSP accountability and due diligence in clause 5, public LSP/DLA disclosure in clause 8(iv)(b), and DLA reporting to RBI in clause 17. It does not use the superseded 2022 board-approved LSP list formulation.
substanceCorroboration: nishithdesai.com analysis of RBI Digital Lending Directions 2025
lawrbit.com summary of Digital Lending Directions 2025
synergialegal.com: Digital Lending Directions 2025 — LSP website disclosure and CIMS reporting requirements
ruleSubstance: The 2025 Directions require REs to: (a) maintain an updated public website listing all engaged LSPs and DLAs; (b) report all DLAs to RBI's CIMS (Centralised Information Management System) portal; (c) take full responsibility for all actions of their engaged LSPs. The RE must ensure all LSPs comply with applicable RBI directions. The 'board-approved list' language from Para 8 of the superseded 2022 Guidelines has evolved — the 2025 Directions focus on disclosure and CIMS reporting rather than a private board-approved list.
implementationDesignNote: This gate is internal-structural, not a legal RE-LSP contract verification. The regulatory substance (RE must maintain LSP accountability and disclose all engaged partners) is current under the 2025 Directions. The specific gate mechanism (internal approved-partners registry keyed on actorId) is an implementation choice of this system, operationalising the RE's accountability obligation as a pre-release check. Any FINANCING_PROVIDER actor not in the registry is treated as an undisclosed/unvouched LSP engagement.
observableGraphCondition: Any Actor with type=FINANCING_PROVIDER in the full proposedGraph whose actorId is not present in .regulatory/approved-partners.json.
implementationNotes: Check is performed against the FULL proposedGraph (not just delta) to catch actors silently added in a prior un-reviewed change.
Adding a partner to approved-partners.json is an explicit compliance team action — it must not be automated.
The 2025 Directions have restructured the old 2022 board-approved-list concept into current due-diligence, accountability, disclosure, and reporting obligations.

Note on old citation error: previous implementation incorrectly cited the clause text of 2022 Para 8 — the quote about data localisation was used as the source for the board-approved list requirement. These are distinct sub-clauses even in the 2022 document.
